summary: Specifies the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP), a message-oriented transport protocol that offers reliable delivery with features such as multiple streams and multihoming. It obsoletes RFC 4960 and folds in the chunk flags registry from RFC 6096 and the I bit of DATA chunks from RFC 7053. It also obsoletes the errata documents RFC 4460 and RFC 8540. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Think of a delivery service that sends many separate parcels at once and can use more than one road. If one parcel gets stuck, the others still arrive.

questions: how does sctp differ from tcp
how does the sctp four-way handshake work
what is a state cookie in sctp
subtitle: A message-oriented, multi-streamed, multihomed transport protocol that fixes several of TCP's limits.

tldr.problem: TCP forces strict ordering on all data, treats traffic as an unstructured byte stream, ties a connection to one address on each side, and is exposed to SYN attacks. Telephone signaling carried over IP needed to avoid all four limits.
tldr.mechanism: SCTP sets up an association between two endpoints with a four-way cookie handshake. It sends discrete messages as chunks in packets that carry a verification tag and a CRC32c checksum. Messages travel in independent streams, and each endpoint can be reachable at several addresses.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9260 is the current specification of SCTP. It obsoletes RFC 4960 and folds in RFC 6096 and RFC 7053, and the errata documents RFC 4460 and RFC 8540 are obsoleted too.

today: RFC 9260 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2022. It obsoletes RFC 4960, RFC 6096, RFC 7053, RFC 4460 and RFC 8540, and no later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why SCTP Exists
sections.content:
The Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) is a reliable transport protocol that runs on top of a connectionless packet network such as IP. It was originally designed to carry Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) signaling messages over IP networks, and the RFC notes that it also suits other uses, for example WebRTC data channels.

The motivation section lists four things applications found too limiting in RFC 793: TCP gives both reliability and strict order of delivery, so head-of-line blocking causes needless delay; its byte-stream nature forces applications to add their own record marking; its sockets complicate highly available multi-homed data transfer; and it is relatively vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks such as SYN attacks.

SCTP therefore offers acknowledged, error-free, non-duplicated transfer of user data, fragmentation to fit the path MTU, sequenced delivery within multiple streams (with an option for order-of-arrival delivery), optional bundling of several user messages into one packet, and network-level fault tolerance through multi-homing. The design also includes congestion avoidance and resistance to flooding and masquerade attacks.

Its central object is the association, a broader concept than a TCP connection. Each endpoint gives the other a list of transport addresses (IP addresses combined with one SCTP port), and the association covers every source and destination combination from those lists. Two endpoints MUST NOT have more than one association between them at a time. SCTP packets can also be carried inside UDP (RFC 6951) or DTLS (RFC 8261).
sections.eli5: Sometimes TCP is too strict, like a single-file line where one slow person holds up everyone. SCTP lets many lines move at once and lets you use more than one road to get there.

sections.title: Packets, Chunks and Parameters
sections.content:
An SCTP packet is a common header followed by one or more chunks. The common header has a 16-bit Source Port Number, a 16-bit Destination Port Number, a 32-bit Verification Tag and a 32-bit Checksum. Port number 0 MUST NOT be used. The checksum is CRC32c. All integer fields are sent in network byte order.

Each chunk has a Chunk Type (8 bits), Chunk Flags (8 bits), a 16-bit Chunk Length and a variable Chunk Value. A chunk with an empty value has length 4. Chunks are padded with zero bytes to a multiple of 4 bytes, and the padding is not counted in the length. The two highest bits of the chunk type say what a receiver does with a type it does not know: stop processing the packet or skip the chunk, and in each case either report it or not. Control chunks carry optional fields as Type-Length-Value parameters with the same kind of rule for unknown types.

The DATA chunk carries user data. Its flags are I (ask the receiver to send a SACK without delay), U (unordered), B (first fragment) and E (last fragment). It also holds a 32-bit TSN, a 16-bit Stream Identifier, a 16-bit Stream Sequence Number and a 32-bit Payload Protocol Identifier. An unfragmented message has both B and E set to 1.

INIT, INIT ACK and SHUTDOWN COMPLETE chunks MUST NOT be bundled with any other chunk. A packet with an INIT chunk MUST have a zero Verification Tag.
sections.eli5: A packet is an envelope with a stamp that shows who it is for and a secret number only the real sender knows. Inside are little cards called chunks, and each card says what it is for.

sections.title: Setting Up an Association
sections.content:
Setup is a four-way handshake. Endpoint A sends INIT with its Initiate Tag and enters COOKIE-WAIT. Endpoint Z answers INIT ACK carrying its own tag and a State Cookie, and MUST NOT allocate resources or keep state for the new association at that point. A returns the cookie in COOKIE ECHO and enters COOKIE-ECHOED. Only when Z receives a valid cookie does it build its state, move to ESTABLISHED and reply COOKIE ACK.

The cookie holds everything Z needs to create the association, plus a message authentication code (MAC) for integrity protection. Using a MAC is mandatory to prevent denial-of-service attacks, and the secret key SHOULD be changed reasonably often. The cookie SHOULD also carry a timestamp and lifespan. On a COOKIE ECHO, Z checks the MAC, the ports and tag, and the age, and sends a "Stale Cookie" error if it has expired. The last two legs of the handshake MAY carry user data.

Streams are fixed at startup. Each side states how many outbound streams it wants and how many inbound it allows. Neither value may be zero, and each side uses the minimum of what was requested and what was offered. Addresses are also exchanged in INIT and INIT ACK as IPv4 or IPv6 Address parameters. If none are present, the packet's source address is the only address of that peer. The deprecated Host Name Address parameter MUST NOT be sent, and a receiver MUST answer with ABORT.

The RFC also covers duplicate and unexpected setup chunks, for example a peer that crashed and restarted, or both sides starting at once.
sections.eli5: Before talking, A knocks and Z hands back a sealed note without writing anything down. A shows the note back, and only then does Z believe A is real and open the door. That way pranksters cannot make Z remember lots of fake visitors.

sections.title: Streams, Acknowledgements and Retransmission
sections.content:
Every DATA chunk has a 32-bit Transmission Sequence Number (TSN) used for reliability, and ordered messages also get a 16-bit Stream Sequence Number used for order within one stream. Because the two are separate, reliable delivery stays functionally separate from sequenced stream delivery. A stream blocked waiting for a missing message does not stop other streams, and a message sent with the U bit set is delivered as soon as it is reassembled.

A receiver acknowledges with a SACK chunk holding a Cumulative TSN Ack, an a_rwnd (receive window), and zero or more Gap Ack Blocks that report TSNs received after a gap, plus duplicate TSNs. The RFC's example shows TSNs 10, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 17 arriving, which gives Cumulative TSN Ack = 12 and two blocks. Acknowledgements SHOULD be generated for at least every second packet and within 200 ms of an unacknowledged DATA chunk arriving. The SACK.Delay parameter MUST NOT be configured above 500 ms.

Timers follow TCP closely. The sender keeps a retransmission timer T3-rtx and an RTO per destination address, computed from a smoothed round-trip time and its variation, and doubles the RTO when the timer expires. Karn's algorithm applies: RTT is not measured from retransmitted chunks. Messages too large for one packet are fragmented into DATA chunks with strictly sequential TSNs, and several chunks may be bundled in one packet. Data stays tied to the association through the 32-bit Verification Tag and CRC32c checksum.
sections.eli5: Each parcel gets a number, and the receiver sends back a note saying which numbers arrived and which are missing. If a parcel is missing for too long, the sender mails it again.

sections.title: Congestion Control
sections.content:
SCTP's congestion control is based on RFC 5681 and is applied to the whole association, not to individual streams. A sender MUST use slow-start and congestion avoidance, and MUST NOT be more aggressive than they allow.

Three variables regulate sending: rwnd (one per association, set by the receiver's buffer space), cwnd and ssthresh. The last two are kept per destination address, together with partial_bytes_acked, so a multi-homed peer gets a separate set of values for each of its addresses. Each address starts with slow start.

After detected loss, ssthresh becomes max(cwnd / 2, 4 * PMDCS) and cwnd is set to that value; on a T3-rtx expiry cwnd falls to one PMDCS. Fast retransmit happens after three miss indications for the same TSN. Congestion control MUST be reinitialized when a DSCP change could put packets in a different queue or when the route changes.

Path MTU discovery follows RFC 8899, with a separate estimate for each destination address. The sender SHOULD also track the smallest Path Maximum DATA Chunk Size across all addresses so that retransmissions can move to an alternate address without IP fragmentation.
sections.eli5: If the road gets jammed, SCTP sends fewer parcels at a time and then slowly speeds up again. Each road has its own speed limit.

sections.title: Multihoming and Fault Management
sections.content:
An endpoint is multi-homed when more than one transport address can reach it. The upper layer picks one as the primary path, and by default the sender transmits there. A timed-out chunk SHOULD be retransmitted to a different active address.

SCTP watches for failures at two levels. It keeps an error counter for each destination address, increased when T3-rtx expires or a HEARTBEAT to an idle address is unanswered within an RTO. When the counter exceeds Path.Max.Retrans, the address is marked inactive and the upper layer is told. It also keeps an association-wide counter against Association.Max.Retrans. When that is exceeded, the peer is considered unreachable and the association closes.

HEARTBEAT chunks are sent periodically to idle addresses to check reachability and the peer must reply with HEARTBEAT ACK, reflecting the opaque information back. The Verification Tag also protects an established association: packets without the expected tag are discarded, which defends against blind masquerade attacks and stale packets from an earlier association.

The RFC suggests values, for example RTO.Initial of 1 second, RTO.Min of 1 second, RTO.Max of 60 seconds, Path.Max.Retrans of 5, Association.Max.Retrans of 10 and HB.interval of 30 seconds.
sections.eli5: If one road is blocked, SCTP notices because little hello messages stop coming back, and it switches to another road. Only when every road is broken does it give up.

sections.title: Association States and Shutdown
sections.content:
An association moves through the states CLOSED, COOKIE-WAIT, COOKIE-ECHOED, ESTABLISHED and then, during shutdown, SHUTDOWN-PENDING, SHUTDOWN-SENT, SHUTDOWN-RECEIVED and SHUTDOWN-ACK-SENT. The RFC's state diagram shows the user commands, received chunks and timeouts that trigger each move.

An association ends by abort or by shutdown. An abort discards any pending data on either end. A shutdown is graceful: the initiator waits in SHUTDOWN-PENDING until its outstanding data is acknowledged, sends SHUTDOWN, and the peer, after finishing what is queued, answers SHUTDOWN ACK. The initiator then sends SHUTDOWN COMPLETE.

SCTP does not support a half-open state like TCP. When either endpoint shuts down, both stop accepting new data from their users and only deliver data already in queue.
sections.eli5: Saying goodbye politely means finishing what you were sending, then both sides say goodbye and hang up. Slamming the phone down is an abort, and anything unsent is lost.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The stated objectives are availability of reliable and timely transport and integrity of the user-to-user information. The design resists flooding through the four-way handshake, the cookie that defers resource commitment until the handshake completes, and the Verification Tag that stops extraneous packets being inserted into an association.

Blind masquerade is made harder because the INIT ACK with the cookie is sent back to the address the INIT came from, so a spoofing attacker does not receive it. For stronger integrity the RFC says SCTP-AUTH (RFC 4895) MAY be used. For confidentiality, user data can be encrypted by the application, for example with DTLS (RFC 6083), or ESP (RFC 4303) can be used, and IKEv2 SHOULD manage its keys.

Implementations MUST handle ICMP as described in the RFC, MUST NOT answer one packet with more than one packet of non-DATA chunks, and MUST abort if a SACK acknowledges a TSN that was never sent. They SHOULD keep INIT ACK chunks small to reduce byte amplification.
sections.eli5: The sealed-note trick and the secret number on every envelope make it hard for strangers to fake a conversation or jam the mailbox.

fields.name: Source Port Number
fields.desc: Sender's port; 0 MUST NOT be used.

fields.name: Destination Port Number
fields.desc: Used to demultiplex to the right endpoint; 0 MUST NOT be used.

fields.name: Verification Tag
fields.desc: Initiate Tag received from the peer; zero in a packet with an INIT chunk.

messages.label: INIT
messages.note: Carries A's Initiate Tag; A enters COOKIE-WAIT.

messages.label: INIT ACK
messages.note: Carries Z's tag and the State Cookie; Z keeps no state.

messages.label: COOKIE ECHO
messages.note: Returns the cookie; A enters COOKIE-ECHOED.

messages.label: COOKIE ACK
messages.note: Z built its state and is ESTABLISHED.

transitions.label: valid COOKIE ECHO: send COOKIE ACK
receive INIT ACK: send COOKIE ECHO
no more outstanding data: send SHUTDOWN
no more outstanding data: send SHUTDOWN ACK
receive SHUTDOWN ACK: send SHUTDOWN COMPLETE
